findings.title: Incorrect update in the function handle_action_token_out()
findings.description:
The function handle_action_token_out() updates the total_amount field when processing output tokens but fails to correctly update the corresponding used_percent field, leading to a state inconsistency in the token tracking mechanism. 
The root cause is the omission of used_percent recalculation after modifying total_amount, which breaks the invariant that used_percent should reflect the ratio of used_amount to total_amount. 
An attacker could exploit this by crafting a multi-hop swap where a token's total_amount is increased via an outflow action without adjusting used_percent, causing it to become disproportionately high. 
This could result in a denial of service (DoS), as subsequent valid actions may miscalculate available token percentages, leading to arithmetic overflows or failed validations when used_percent exceeds 10,000.

findings.title: Lack of handling pumpfun sell operation in swap_v3() function
findings.description:
The swap_v3() function processes complex multi-hop swap operations but does not implement proper handling logic for pumpfun sell operations, specifically failing to process the native SOL received from such operations. 
The cause is the absence of dedicated code paths or balance checks for SOL transfers when a PumpfunSell protocol is involved in a single-hop swap. 
An attacker or user could trigger a swap involving a pumpfun sell, leading to incorrect balance calculations or failure to transfer received SOL to the intended recipient. 
The impact is that the function may fail during execution, resulting in a loss of user funds or a denial of service for swaps involving pumpfun sell operations.
